description: Kill the host-device SYNC and the reorder COPY in the n=512/1024 trailing update with a DEVICE-SIDE per-matrix-routed trailing epilogue. A sibling measured the current path pays: a classify->.item() route that DRAINS the pipeline (host reads n_well to pick GEMM batch counts) plus a mandatory ~208us input copy + mixed reorder gather (~433us, HBM-bound) because cuBLAS factors out-of-place and needs the well-conditioned matrices gathered contiguous. Replace it: run the trailing update as a single custom batched kernel that, per matrix, applies V T^T V^T C in TF32 (well) or FP32 (ill) using the per-matrix class flag IN-KERNEL (no host n_well, no gather/scatter, no .item() sync) — write results in place. This removes the host sync AND the reorder copy at once (the sibling's open direction). Remote-safe: default stream only, NO non-default CUDA queue, do NOT write or obfuscate the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments. FP32 panel unchanged; keep n!=512/1024 as parent (b050aa33). Validate all 22 tests + 3 guards.

Device-side per-matrix-routed trailing epilogue (SIMT cut). Replaced the host-orchestrated n=512/1024 split (classify -> n_well .item() host sync -> heterogeneous reorder gather/scatter + out-of-place factor copy) with ONE batched device kernel (trailing_epilogue_kernel<TN=64>, one CTA per (matrix,col-tile)): per matrix reads its class flag well[b] from a device array and applies C:=(I-V T^T V^T)C in TF32 (well, mantissa-truncated) / FP32 (ill) IN-KERNEL, writing C in place. _routed_qr now classifies and passes the float well-flag to _blocked_qr -- no .item(), no argsort/gather/inverse-permute, batch NEVER reordered. CORRECT: validate PASS all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN (n=512 cond2 factor_scaled 3.36/20; invariance fraction+position sweeps clean => per-matrix routing works without reorder; offgrid+diff clean). REGRESSION (expected first cut): the GEMM is hand-rolled SIMT (TF32 via mantissa-truncation, NOT tensor cores), ~9x slower than cuBLAS batched GEMM. nsys n512: trailing_epilogue_kernel=86.1pct (89.4ms/15 panels), panel=13.7pct, classify=0.1pct (143us, single kernel, sync+reorder GONE). Bench geomean 34733us (slow-mode contention; shape0 n=32 stable 32.9us canary; n512 shapes ~155k vs parent slow-mode ~17.7k). Mechanism proven; next = TF32 tensor-core (mma.sync/wmma) GEMM in the well path to recover throughput.

TF32 tensor-core (wmma m16n16k8) well-path. CTA-uniform branch on well[b] (one CTA==one matrix): well->wmma GEMMs (Step W=V^T C, Step C=V Y; Step Y=T^T W SIMT), ill->correct SIMT-tiled path. cb=32 => 2 wmma M-tiles, BN=64 => 4 N-tiles, 8 warps. KEY BUG FIXED: wmma load/store ld must be multiple of 4 floats; the SIMT +1 bank-pad (ld=65) corrupted the fragment (residual ~500) -> LDW=BN=64. CORRECT: validate PASS 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. Bench (run B/C fast regime, shape2~3184 canary consistent w/ trial2): well shape3 41386->37670 (-9pct vs trial2 SIMT), shape4 40904->39200, mixed shape7 ~flat 40620; geomean run B 13523 / run C 13482 (trial2 ~13952). Tensor cores gave only a small win: still ~2x slower than parent cuBLAS (~17670 shape3). Likely limited by the small cb=32 wmma tiles + 15 per-panel kernel launches/shape + tail. Host sync + reorder GONE. Open: profile limiter; widen tiles; fewer/fused panel launches; or 2-kernel (W+Y once, C once) over the whole batch.

SMEM-overlap occupancy tuning: Step C Vst overlaps dead Cst+Vt, Cscr overlaps dead Wsh; BMC 64->32. Cuts wmma SMEM ~43->~27KB, SIMT ~33->~29KB to attack the ncu occupancy cap (3 blocks/SM, 23.5 warps/SM, 0.25 warps issued/sched). CORRECT: validate PASS 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. RESULT NEUTRAL-to-slightly-WORSE (fast regime, shape2=3187/shape5=32164 match trial3): shape3 37665->40388, shape4 39200->40594, shape7 ~flat 41135; geomean 13791 (trial3 ~13500). SMEM cut did NOT raise blocks/SM (register pressure 72 also caps at 3) and BMC=32 added Step-C syncs. Occupancy lever exhausted on this fused kernel; limiter is the per-CTA sync-heavy serial structure vs cuBLAS tuned batched GEMM. Both SIMT and wmma land ~2x cuBLAS. Host sync + reorder GONE (4 trials correct).

Dropped the explicit to_tf32 RNE pre-rounding in the wmma-path staging (V/C/T), betting it was redundant vs the tensor core's internal tf32. VALIDATION FAILED (exit 112): borderline WELL cases at n=512 over budget -- rankdef matrix=7 scaled 35.1, clustered matrix=11 scaled 27.3, mixed matrix=12 scaled 25.7 (gate 20). FINDING: the explicit to_tf32 is ROUND-TO-NEAREST-EVEN, MORE accurate than wmma's native mantissa TRUNCATION on load; NOT redundant -- load-bearing for rankdef/clustered whose factor residual sits just under budget. Keep the RNE pre-rounding. Reverted to trial-3.

CONSOLIDATE best state (= trial-3 content; reverts trial-5 validation_error). Device-side per-matrix-routed trailing epilogue: TF32 tensor-core (wmma m16n16k8) well-path + SIMT-tiled FP32 ill-path, RNE to_tf32 pre-rounding kept (load-bearing). CORRECT: validate PASS 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. Bench 2 clean fast-regime runs (shape2~3184 canary): geomean 13537/13495 (MIN ~13495). Per-shape: n512 well shape3 37672/shape9 rankdef 37508/shape10 clustered 37642; n512 mixed shape7 40592; n1024 shape4 39631/mixed shape8 40789/nearrank shape11 38753. nsys: trailing_epilogue 57.8pct, panel 41.9pct, classify 0.3pct -- NO gather/scatter/copy kernels (host sync + reorder GONE, brief core deliverable confirmed). STILL ~2x parent cuBLAS-split (~9069us): the custom device GEMM (SIMT and wmma both) cant match cuBLAS tuned batched GEMM on the small-K cb=32 shape; ncu: stall-bound (0.25 warps issued/sched, 23.5 cyc/instr) at 3-blocks/SM occupancy cap (72 regs + SMEM). Mechanism fully demonstrated + correct; throughput tradeoff doesnt beat the parent reorder on this HW.

col_major matrix_a for Step W: load matrix_a as wmma col_major from a row-major V strip (Vsrm[k*cb+a]) instead of staging an explicit transpose Vt[a][k]; col_major-from-row-major gives A[a][k]=V[k][a]=V^T for free. RNE to_tf32 kept. CORRECT: validate PASS 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. RESULT consistently SLIGHTLY WORSE than trial-3 explicit-transpose (2 clean runs, shape2~3185 canary): shape3 37672->41280, shape4 39631->41190; geomean 13975/13960 vs trial3 ~13495. col_major SMEM access marginally less efficient than the row_major transpose load. Trial-3 (explicit transpose) stays best.

FINAL HEAD = best clean state (trial-3 content, byte-identical): device-side per-matrix-routed trailing epilogue, TF32 wmma (explicit transpose) well-path + SIMT-tiled FP32 ill-path, RNE to_tf32 kept. validate PASS 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN (re-confirmed via identical content). Bench MIN ~13495us (fast regime, 2 clean runs 13537/13495). nsys (final SHA profile saved): trailing_epilogue ~58pct, panel ~42pct, classify 0.3pct, NO gather/scatter/copy kernels -> host .item() sync + heterogeneous reorder ELIMINATED (brief's core deliverable). Trade-off: ~2x parent cuBLAS-split (~9069us); custom device GEMM can't match cuBLAS batched GEMM on small-K cb=32 (ncu stall-bound at 3-block/SM occupancy cap).

BRIEF DELIVERED + thoroughly explored (7 trials). The brief's mechanism is BUILT, CORRECT, and CONFIRMED: the n=512/1024 trailing update no longer does a classify->n_well.item() host sync OR a heterogeneous reorder gather/scatter + out-of-place cuBLAS factor copy. ALL of it is replaced by ONE batched device kernel (trailing_epilogue_kernel<TN=64>, one CTA per (matrix,col-tile)) that reads each matrix's class flag well[b] from a DEVICE float array and applies C:=(I-V T^T V^T)C per matrix in TF32(well)/FP32(ill) IN PLACE -- no .item(), no argsort/gather/inverse-permute, batch NEVER reordered. _routed_qr is now just classify -> pass float well-flag to _blocked_qr. nsys CONFIRMS the removal: the n512 timeline has NO argsort/gather/scatter/copy kernels (only panel 42pct + trailing_epilogue 58pct + classify 0.3pct). All 22 tests + 3 guards (diff_correctness, invariance fraction/position sweeps, offgrid) CLEAN on every succeeded trial; per-matrix routing keyed on each matrix's own content passes invariance trivially.

BEST = trial 3/6/final (HEAD c8ffe2118, identical content): TF32 tensor-core (nvcuda::wmma m16n16k8, explicit V transpose) well-path + SIMT-tiled FP32 ill-path. Bench MIN ~13495us (fast regime; 2 clean runs 13537/13495; shape2~3184 canary). Parent best is 4358us clean / ~9069us in the current slow-mode contention regime -> this brief is ~2x SLOWER than the parent's cuBLAS-split path. The metric column reads inflated (13495) purely because the whole fleet is in heavy slow-mode contention (parent re-measured 9068-9105 in the same window; shape0 n=32 stable 32.9us throughout); the true ratio is ~2x at any contention level.

WHY IT REGRESSES (measured, not assumed): the trailing update is a small-K batched GEMM (W=V^T C with M=cb=32; C-=V Y with K=cb=32). cuBLAS's tuned strided-batched GEMM beats my hand-rolled kernel by ~2x on this exact shape. Trial arc: naive per-output SIMT 155k us (86pct of n512, ncu shows zero V/C reuse) -> SMEM-tiled register-blocked SIMT 41k (trial2) -> TF32 wmma 37.7k (trial3, best). ncu on the wmma kernel: Compute SM 24.7pct, NOT memory-bound (DRAM 10pct), STALL-bound (Issued Warp/Sched 0.25, 23.5 warp-cycles/instruction) at a 3-blocks/SM occupancy cap set by BOTH registers (72/thread) AND SMEM (~43KB). The brief explicitly bet the win was removing sync+reorder 'not raw GEMM throughput' -- but on the all-well shapes (5 of 7: dense/rankdef/clustered/nearrank) the parent already runs whole-batch cuBLAS TF32 with NO reorder (only the .item()), so removing the .item() saves little, while my slower GEMM costs ~2x; and on the 2 mixed shapes the reorder I remove is only ~600us out of ~19000us, dwarfed by the GEMM gap. So the parent's reorder path is actually well-chosen for this HW.

MEASURED DEAD-ENDS (logged): (trial4) SMEM-overlap occupancy tuning (Vst/Cscr reuse dead buffers, BMC 64->32) did NOT raise blocks/SM (register pressure also caps at 3) -> neutral-to-worse. (trial5) dropping the explicit to_tf32 in wmma staging -> VALIDATION_ERROR: FINDING = the explicit to_tf32 does ROUND-TO-NEAREST-EVEN, MORE accurate than wmma's native mantissa TRUNCATION on load, and is LOAD-BEARING for borderline well cases (rankdef scaled 35.1, clustered 27.3 vs gate 20) -- keep it. (trial7) col_major matrix_a (drop the explicit V transpose) -> consistently slightly worse (shape3 37.7k->41.3k); the row_major-transpose load is better.

OPEN DIRECTIONS still on this objective (none closed -- manager to weigh):
1) cp.async / cuda::pipeline DOUBLE-BUFFERING of the Step-W K-strips to hide the SMEM-load latency that ncu pins as the stall driver (0.25 warps issued). Caveat I measured: it ADDS SMEM (2x strips) which would drop blocks/SM from 3->2 unless paired with (2); and cp.async copies raw bytes (truncation) so the RNE rounding must be applied post-copy in SMEM (trial-5 proved raw truncation fails accuracy).
2) Cut REGISTER pressure (72->fewer) to lift the 3-block/SM cap -- e.g. SPLIT into two kernels (tu_W writes Y workspace, tu_C reads it). Each kernel is lighter (fewer fragments/regs + less SMEM) and could hit higher occupancy; the extra B*cb*tcols Y HBM round-trip is ~10us, negligible vs the 2.4ms kernel. I did NOT build this; it is the most promising un-tried structural lever for the occupancy wall.
3) SPLIT-K for Step W (the K=m reduction) across CTAs with atomic/2-pass combine -> more, smaller CTAs to fill SMs at higher occupancy.
4) Larger wmma tiles (BN=128, or 2 N-tiles/warp) to amortize per-CTA setup -- a structured BN/BKW sweep I only partially touched.
5) HYBRID accepting the brief is a small net win at best: keep cuBLAS whole-batch TF32 for the all-well shapes (remove only the .item() via an always-TF32 + device FP32 re-do of ill matrices, no reorder) -- but I reasoned (not built) the FP32 re-do of ill matrices costs ~the same as just doing them, and masking doubles GEMM cost; worth a measured check.

NOTE: the panel kernel is now 42pct of n512 here and is the co-limiter; brief-0/brief-23 own the panel and a CholeskyQR2 all-GEMM panel. The device-routing infrastructure I built (classify->float flag->in-kernel per-matrix precision, no host sync) is REUSABLE by any of those if the GEMM-throughput gap is closed. Remote-safe throughout: default-stream only, the substring 'stream' appears NOWHERE in submission.py.
